old: "To explain external drivers of movement, Hungarian uses causal postpositions: *miatt* ('because of'), *folytán* ('as a consequence of' - usually with instrumental *-val/-vel*), and *következtében* ('as a result of' - preceded by the noun's unmarked or possessive form)."
new: "You know *miatt* ('because of') from earlier units and *következtében* ('as a result of') from B1 Unit 31. To explain external drivers of movement, all three causal postpositions follow the plain noun: *a háború miatt*, *a háború következtében* and the new *folytán* ('as a consequence of'): *a háború folytán*."
why: miatt/következtében known (Unit 31); folytán does not take -val/-vel; "possessive form" claim wrong

old: "Both *ellenére* and *dacára* express 'in spite of / despite'. They take the possessive or unmarked form: *a nehézségek ellenére* ('despite the difficulties'), *a honvágy dacára* ('in spite of homesickness')."
new: "You know *annak ellenére, hogy* from B1 Unit 9. The postpositions *ellenére* and *dacára* both express 'in spite of / despite' and follow the plain noun: *a nehézségek ellenére* ('despite the difficulties'), *a honvágy dacára* ('in spite of homesickness')."
why: recap annak ellenére, hogy; "possessive form" claim wrong

old: "*Miközben / mialatt* ('while / as') introduce temporal clauses describing overlapping events. In noun phrases, the postposition *során* ('in the course of / during') governs processes: *az utazás során* ('during the journey')."
new: "You know *miközben* ('while') from B1 Unit 4. *Mialatt* ('while, during the time that') works the same way and introduces temporal clauses describing overlapping events. In noun phrases, the postposition *során* ('in the course of / during') governs processes: *az utazás során* ('during the journey')."

old: "Expressing bicultural identity relies on paired correlatives: *egyszerre... és...* ('at once... and...'), *nemcsak... hanem... is* ('not only... but also...'): *Egyszerre érzi magát európainak és büszke magyarnak.*"
new: "You know *nemcsak … hanem … is* ('not only … but also …') from A2 Unit 5. New here is the pair *egyszerre … és …* ('at once … and …'), which sets two identities side by side: *Egyszerre érzi magát európainak és büszke magyarnak.*"
why: nem csak ... hanem is is A2 Unit 5

new: "*Letelepedik vhol* ('settles down somewhere': *-on/-en/-ön* or *-ban/-ben*, as you know them from A1), *beilleszkedik a társadalomba* ('integrates into society': *-ba/-be*, A1 Unit 12) and *alkalmazkodik a helyi szokásokhoz* ('adapts to local customs': *-hoz/-hez/-höz*; you know *alkalmazkodik vmihez* from B1 Unit 49)."

old: "Complex descriptive discourse links multiple relative clauses: *Az a könyv, amelyet tavaly olvastam, és amely olyan mély nyomot hagyott bennem...* Note agreement between the head demonstrative (*az, azok*) and relative pronouns (*aki, ami, amely*)."
new: "You know the relative pronouns *aki*, *ami* and *amely* from A2 Unit 4 and their case forms from B1 Unit 21. In careful speech and writing several relative clauses are chained with *és*: *Az a könyv, amelyet tavaly olvastam, és amely olyan mély nyomot hagyott bennem...* Note agreement between the head demonstrative (*az, azok*) and the relative pronouns (*aki, ami, amely*)."
why: relative clauses are A2 Unit 4 / B1 Unit 21: recap, new part is the chain

old: "*Amely* is the formal, literary relative pronoun ('which / that'). *Amelyik* is selective ('which one of several'): *a festmény, amely a falon függ* ('the painting which hangs on the wall') vs *Válaszd azt a könyvet, amelyik a legjobban tetszik!* ('Choose that book which you like best!')."
new: "You know *amely* ('which / that') from A2 Unit 4; it is the formal, literary relative pronoun. New here is *amelyik*, which is selective ('which one of several'): *a festmény, amely a falon függ* ('the painting which hangs on the wall') vs *Válaszd azt a könyvet, amelyik a legjobban tetszik!* ('Choose that book which you like best!')."

old: "The suffix *-hatatlan/-hetetlen* corresponds to '-able/-ible' with negation ('un-...-able'): *felejthetetlen* ('unforgettable'), *megingathatatlan* ('unshakeable'), *megmagyarázhatatlan* ('unexplainable'), *pótolhatatlan* ('irreplaceable')."
new: "The suffix *-hatatlan/-hetetlen* is built on the potential *-hat/-het* you know from A2 Unit 23 and means 'un-...-able' ('cannot be ...ed'): *felejthetetlen* ('unforgettable'), *megingathatatlan* ('unshakeable'), *megmagyarázhatatlan* ('unexplainable'), *pótolhatatlan* ('irreplaceable')."
why: -hat/-het potential is A2 Unit 23; these are adjectives, not participles
